description: Closed circle of suspects with alibis — find the contradiction to identify the culprit
puzzle_mechanic: Alibi contradiction and logical elimination. Each suspect has an alibi; the culprit's alibi contains a subtle inconsistency revealed by cross-referencing 2+ evidence files. Solver must eliminate suspects whose alibis are verified and find the one whose alibi breaks.

difficulty_scaling.easy: 4 suspects, 1 alibi obviously weak, single cross-reference needed to break it
difficulty_scaling.medium: 4-5 suspects, 2 suspects have weak-looking alibis (one is genuine), requires 2+ cross-references
difficulty_scaling.hard: 5 suspects, culprit has strongest-looking alibi (contradiction deeply embedded), requires 3+ cross-references across scattered evidence

generation_prompt:
You are generating a CLASSIC WHODUNIT mystery scenario.

Core mechanic: ALIBI CONTRADICTION. Every suspect has an alibi. The culprit's alibi appears solid but contains a subtle inconsistency that can only be found by cross-referencing multiple evidence files.

Evidence design rules:
- Each suspect should have at least 1 evidence file that seems to support their alibi
- The culprit's alibi evidence must contain a specific factual detail that contradicts another evidence file (e.g., timestamps that don't match, locations that are impossible given travel time, witnesses who couldn't have seen what they claim)
- Red herrings should make innocent suspects look suspicious (financial trouble, relationship conflicts, etc.) but their alibis should ultimately hold up
- Include at least one timeline or schedule document that serves as the 'key' to breaking the alibi
- Witness statements should be slightly different from each other (realistic inconsistency) but only the culprit-related inconsistency should be logically significant

The answer.motive should explain WHY the culprit did it. The answer.method should explain HOW (weapon, poison, action).
visual_style: Drawing room, candlelight, rain on windows, suspect lineup, vintage mystery

example_outline.title: The Midnight Banquet
example_outline.setting: Private restaurant VIP room, midnight dinner party
example_outline.incident: Wealthy diner found poisoned during a private dinner party
example_outline.motive_hint: Inheritance dispute — victim was changing his will
example_outline.method_hint: Poison in decanted wine during sommelier's preparation
example_outline.key_contradiction: C claims he left the VIP room at 11:15 but CCTV shows the corridor empty at that time
